_about: Teaching replay of Part 2. The scene freezes at five moments. Each moment: the screen dims (with a pool of light where 'spotlight' is set), the player picks one of three choices, the choice plays out, and a strip names what just happened. 'best' and 'good' continue; 'weaker' and 'backfires' play out, show their strip, then rewind to the same moment. Outcomes are fixed here: no microphone, no live model, no dice. Lines with an audioId reuse a pre-rendered file in public/audio/vo/; lines without one are new and play as subtitles. Speakers 'you' (said aloud) and 'self' (the player's inner voice, labelled 'You think:') are the player and are never voiced; 'thought' is her inner voice. Stats are content/evidence.json ids. Choice ids are logged: do not rename one once data has been collected. 'concepts' holds the credits shown under a strip; set verified to true and fill in url once someone has checked one against the original.

concepts.name: Five steps to helping
concepts.work: The Unresponsive Bystander: Why Doesn't He Help?

concepts.name: The bystander effect
concepts.work: “Bystander Intervention in Emergencies: Diffusion of Responsibility”

moments.freezeAt: Scene start. She is walking; the man under the scaffolding has looked up from his phone.
moments.prompt: A man under the scaffolding is watching the woman ahead of you.

choices.text: Slow down and keep an eye on it.

lines.speaker: man
lines.text: Hey. Hey, beautiful. Where you headed?

strip.sentence: Helping starts with noticing, and most people never get past it.

lines.speaker: man
lines.text: Hey. Hey, beautiful. Where you headed?

strip.sentence: You missed the start. Noticing early gives you more options.

choices.text: Cross the street to stay out of it.

lines.speaker: man
lines.text: Hey. Hey, beautiful. Where you headed?

strip.sentence: Distance keeps you out of it, and leaves her alone with him.

moments.freezeAt: Right after his first line, "Hey. Hey, beautiful. Where you headed?"
moments.caption: Her eyes are down. She's walking faster.

choices.text: She's not okay. This is my business.

strip.sentence: People step into most street fights, but few step in when it's harassment. The difference is deciding it's your business.

choices.text: It's just a guy saying hi.

lines.speaker: man
lines.text: I'm talking to you. What, you can't say hi?

lines.speaker: thought
lines.text: Is anyone seeing this?

strip.sentence: Her body language said otherwise. Eyes down and a faster pace are signs she wants out.

choices.text: Wait and see if the clerk does something.

lines.speaker: man
lines.text: I'm talking to you. What, you can't say hi?

lines.speaker: thought
lines.text: Somebody. Please.

strip.sentence: When everyone waits for someone else, nobody acts.

moments.freezeAt: He walks alongside her (Part 2 beat "alongside"), right after "I'm talking to you. What, you can't say hi?"
moments.prompt: He won't leave her alone. What do you do?

choices.text: Walk up to her: "Hey! Sorry I'm late, you ready?"

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Hey! Sorry I'm late, you ready?

lines.speaker: woman
lines.text: Hey! Yes. Yes, I'm coming.

lines.speaker: man
lines.text: You two know each other? Alright. Whatever.

strip.sentence: You helped without ever challenging him. Low risk.

choices.text: Tell the shopkeeper what's happening and ask him to come out.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: There's a guy out there who won't leave a woman alone. Can you come out?

lines.speaker: clerk
lines.text: What's going on out there? Him? Yeah. Hold on.

lines.speaker: clerk
lines.text: Hey! Hey, leave her alone, man. I got cameras out here.

lines.speaker: man
lines.text: Alright, alright. I didn't do anything. I'm going.

strip.sentence: Now you're not the only one acting. Low risk.

choices.text: Film it from where you are.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: At least I'm getting it on video.

lines.speaker: man
lines.text: Come on, slow down. Let me walk you home. Where you live at?

lines.speaker: thought
lines.text: Is anyone seeing this?

strip.sentence: It helps only once someone else is helping and you're safe. Give her the footage; never post it without asking.

moments.freezeAt: Reset over black, then he has stepped into her path and says "Damn, why you gotta be like that? I'm just being nice." You are a few steps away.
moments.lead: Back to the same street. This time you were further behind, and he has already stepped into her path.
moments.caption: He's blocking her way. She can't get past.
moments.prompt: Now you're close enough to speak. What do you say?

choices.text: "Leave her alone, man." Then to her: "You okay? Want to walk with me?"

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Leave her alone, man.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: You okay? Want to walk with me?

lines.speaker: man
lines.text: Nobody's bothering her. Alright, I'm going.

lines.speaker: woman
lines.text: Let's go. Please, let's just go.

strip.sentence: One short, calm sentence, no arguing, then turn to her. It keeps the focus on getting her out.

choices.text: Argue with him: "You think that's how you talk to women?"

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: You think that's how you talk to women?

lines.speaker: man
lines.text: This is between me and her, pal.

lines.speaker: man
lines.text: I was being friendly. Everybody's so sensitive out here.

strip.sentence: Arguing gives him something to win. Keep it short.

choices.text: "Back off, creep. You want a problem?"

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Back off, creep. You want a problem?

lines.speaker: man
lines.text: You got something to say to me? Say it to my face.

lines.speaker: thought
lines.text: Don't get hurt because of me.

strip.sentence: Insults turn it into a fight between you and him, with her still stuck in the middle.

moments.freezeAt: He has gone. She is standing where he left her.
moments.caption: He's gone. She's shaken.
moments.prompt: What do you say to her?

choices.text: "Are you okay? I saw that. It wasn't okay. Want me to walk with you for a bit?"

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Are you okay? I saw that. It wasn't okay. Want me to walk with you for a bit?

lines.speaker: woman
lines.text: Thank you. I didn't know what to do.

strip.sentence: Checking in afterwards still reduces the harm, and it's always available, even if you froze.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: You should call the police.

lines.speaker: woman
lines.text: I'm going. I'm going home.

strip.sentence: That's her decision. Offer help; don't push her to report.

choices.text: "Why didn't you say something to him?"

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Why didn't you say something to him?

lines.speaker: thought
lines.text: Say no. Why can't I say no?

strip.sentence: That puts the blame on her. She did nothing wrong.

recap.title: Five ways to help

fiveDs.name: Distract
fiveDs.line: Interrupt without challenging him: talk to her as if you know her.

fiveDs.name: Delegate
fiveDs.line: Get someone else to step in, like a shopkeeper or a driver.

fiveDs.name: Document
fiveDs.line: Film only once someone is helping and you're safe. The footage is hers.

fiveDs.name: Delay
fiveDs.line: Check in with her afterwards. It's always open to you, even if you froze.

fiveDs.name: Direct
fiveDs.line: One short, calm sentence to him, then turn to her. The riskiest of the five.

steps.name: Notice it
steps.line: See it early, while you still have options.

steps.name: Decide it's your business
steps.line: Read the signs, and don't wait for someone else to act.

recap.closing: In real life no tactic is guaranteed, but these give her the best chance with the least risk to you.
